source.title: Orthogonal and Parametrized Multi-Attribute Steering of LLMs
source.authors: Remy Ogasawara; C. Anderson; N. Oozeer; Foad Namjoo; Amir Abdullah; J. Schou; Jeff M. Phillips

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports results on interference between correlated LLM steering vectors, but does not test sparse-feature superposition, capacity pressure, SAE feature completeness, or whether model features are one-dimensional. Those steering-vector results are related but do not test any listed version.
record.gate_note: The reported steering-vector results are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version. The paper’s clipping and single-trait steering curves, benchmark results, and dataset-validation results do not measure a claim version. The multi-attribute comparisons are steering-method results, not tests of feature superposition.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes steering methods (clipping, parameterized, orthogonalized multi-trait steering) and reports their performance on correlated contrastive steering vectors in Llama 2 7B Chat and Qwen3-8B. It does not test sparse-feature superposition, capacity-driven polysemanticity, SAE features, or feature dimensionality. It assumes the linear representation hypothesis. All rows compare the authors' methods with α-iterative steering, which is T4/T6-type method performance, not a test of any version. Superposition is not even cited explicitly. 'cites_only' is the closest relation, with T6 tranche.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that clipping the steering range, parameterized steering, and orthogonalizing steering vectors make steering more robust and interpretable. Non-orthogonal multi-trait steering suffers interference (α-iterative) or order dependence (parameterized). Orthogonalization removes order dependence (proved) and reduces interference, but does not eliminate it or fully steer all behaviours.
record.recipe_differences: The cited original source concerns toy networks and feature superposition; this study uses contrastive activation steering and geometric transformations in LLM residual-stream representations. It does not reproduce the original method.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured steering interaction varies with trait-pair correlation, the second trait’s steering strength, steering order for non-orthogonal parameterized methods, and model (Llama 2 7B Chat versus Qwen3-8B).

fits_no_version.finding: Contrastive steering vectors for related behaviours are highly correlated (cosine up to 0.87). Composing them interferes, and projecting to orthogonal coordinates reduces but does not remove the interference. Sycophancy-positive and warmth-negative means stay close after orthogonalization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Correlated linear behaviour directions in LLMs interfere under linear composition; linear orthogonalization reduces but does not eliminate the interaction.

record.problems: The results concern steering-vector interaction rather than feature superposition or capacity. The authors report that orthogonalization does not eliminate interference and note remaining representational proximity for warmth and sycophancy; uncertainty estimates for the reported table values are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted per-trait-pair entries from Tables 2, 3, and 8, and the alternate percent_steered tables in Appendices D, E, and F; retained the reported aggregate results and the motivating warmth/sycophancy comparison. Also omitted Table 4 benchmark steering results because they do not measure the claim-related vector-interference finding.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, sparsity transitions, or feature geometry.
All: no capacity analysis or neuron polysemanticity.
All: no neuron-level analysis and no SAEs trained or evaluated (SAE steering only cited).
All: the study assumes 1-D steering directions and does not test dimensionality.

record.verdict_notes: The relation is changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only': the paper never discusses superposition and relies only on the linear representation hypothesis. No verdicts are given because no row measures anything a version names. The Qwen results show orthogonal parameterized steering (OP) below α-iterative (AI) at β=+1 (0.382 vs 0.616), so the reader's 'partial' states encoded method comparisons rather than version effects.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions; feature overlap, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether capacity limits cause polysemanticity, or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions while others share.
Whether polysemanticity can arise without capacity pressure or whether it is evidence of superposition.
Whether LLM features spread across neurons or are recoverable using a sparse autoencoder.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units of model representation.
Whether superposed model features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features; the study uses one-dimensional steering vectors but does not test feature dimensionality.
